hits.name: Logan Kilpatrick
hits.text:
Today we are rolling out Gemini 4 Argon globally in the Gemini API, to Pro + Ultra in Gemini App, and Ultra subs in Antigravity!

Argon is a huge step forward for Gemini, and a labor of love. This model has been battle tested by over 100,000 people at Google over the last month, with so much new innovation, ambition, and hard work baked into this release. The team has been heads down over the last 6 months working to make this possible across the stack (research, infra, safety, eng, etc).

We rolled the model out to cyber defenders as part of our fairwind program and early access customers over the last 2 weeks, it has been amazing to see and talk to folks who are now using this model daily. Seeing the models writing capability, raw knowledge and persistence for coding, paired with new features like 1M token output when the model needs to work more has gotten me even more excited about our path ahead.

This is just the start of the Gemini 4 era. As you saw with 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash, our iteration speed with Gemini is fast : ) Now with Gemini 4 Argon to work from, I am cannot wait to see the progress continue, and most importantly see what this new model enables for the world. 

This is such a special moment in the arc of technology, as millions of people everyday tackle problems they could never have thought possible before. Gemini 4 Argon was built to help you tackle the hardest problems. I have personally felt this spark with Argon and hope you do too. Onwards!!

This is also interesting to think about

Right now it still takes, let's say, 30 minutes to a few hours to build something usable with AI and then you still polish for days/weeks/months

If we assume this will keep getting faster, at some point an AI model will take a second or less to generate the whole thing

Imagine a future where you can create anything in less than second?

How will that change what we choose to create? Will humans even create, or will it all be AI agents coming up with ideas themselves?

The next constraints then become physical? If AI can generate for example hardware plans so fast, it will still take 30 minutes to 3d print that, so maybe the next speed and intelligence optimizations will then start happening in hardware, being able to generate an idea and producing a physical object in a minute or so

I have no idea but very interesting, it's kinda like those real-time video models we saw last month (like my Infinite Slop project), how will content change if you can generate so fast?

🤔

hits.name: Matt Pocock
hits.text:
Debating adding a GRILL.md file to customize how /grill-me works

A few benefits:

1. /grill-with-docs gets removed, you just have 'invoke the domain-modeling skill' in your GRILL.md and use /grill-me
2. Customize what you care about/get asked about during planning (security, module strategy, etc)
3. Choose whether you want to be grilled one at a time or all together

People seem really, really reticent to actually edit the skill themselves, so this seems sensible to me.

hits.name: Claire Vo
hits.text:
everyone is asking us at @cxodev about calculating ROI on AI, here's what we're saying:
1. focus on engineering, it's 80%+ of your spend - if you're looking to improve cost efficiency its the big lever to move (so stop wasting time in other depts)
2 . model tests + evals are your friend. learn to run them for the most expensive parts of your business
3. spend time with your top spenders: they're either a) doing things your full team should do or b) an easy spot to save some $$$
4. you're probably underspending relative to oppty all things considered
5. PR velocity is a good not great measure of eng ROI. you need to tie to actual product intiatives and use 
6. if you're not sucking up session data + traces you can't really tell if your team is using AI on the right things
7. everyone is blowing through their 12 month budget in 4 months. you're not alone
8. aim for 2-10x improvements in ops efficiency. 30% is a rounding error.
9. time saved =/= ROI. what are you doing with that time?
10. you should be eliminating whole categories of human toil
11. nobody calculated the roi of email. some of this is simple work transformation
12. idk we still like tokenmaxxing
13. you will spike up and then it will be possible to pull down costs (but not output) - we see it all the time. intelligence is getting cheaper.
14. revenue per fully loaded employee is emerging as the north star guide. most leaders won't say that out loud to their teams.
15. spend capping your top users is dumb. they're the ones most likely to be highest impact if you really look.
16. sorry, but you just don't have that many fable-level problems. stop making it your defaut.

what am i missing?

virals_narrative: Outside the watchlist, Mon to Wed noon is Google's turn. Gemini 4 Argon launched on Oct 13 (Sundar Pichai ~4.18M, Logan Kilpatrick ~909K on the watchlist) and the reach went to visual proof, not benchmarks: Demis Hassabis' wizard chess game (~346K), fofr's pelican drawn with Fourier epicycles plus Argon-made video and music (~343K, which Simon Willison quoted), Sundar's thread of a raw Pixel CAD file turned into an exploded-view animation via Blender MCP (~293K), and Min Choi's "people are already building insane 3D worlds" list (~26K). The second wave is cost and loyalty receipts: Theo's "8 years of $200 Claude subs vs a quantized DeepSeek box" (~295K) and "months until anything beats Opus 5.5" (~61K), DHH's Sol at $0.80 vs Opus $10.53 (~44K), Guillermo Rauch's "coding agents are the killer app, stay model agnostic" (~124K) and Riley Brown's "2 frontier models back to back... back to Claude Code and Codex" (~18K). Vibe coding is split between skeptics and satire: "why hasn't anyone vibe coded a YouTube alternative" (~40K), "I don't know a single business that cancelled a subscription for a vibe-coded tool" (~34K) and Santiago's vibe-coded-everything joke (~43K). Underneath sits a diffusion story that fits @bobbyships: Ethan Mollick's legal DDoS of customer service by refund-hunting agents (~190K), Amjad Masad's "pause research today and AI still needs 10 years to diffuse" (~12K), and François Chollet's "millions of AI-aided human scientists, not a few labs" (~33K). Nikita Bier's "every social surface decays into slop" (~124K) and a spam-caps "DON'T USE GEMINI 4 ARGON" post (~106K) show reach bait is still everywhere. Best angles for Adele: Argon proves 3D is now cheap, so point it at something people own (their body); the demo should live inside the post; and the real bottleneck is people understanding, not models building.

drafts.hook: Matt Pocock's 18-line "mistakes you might be making" list (~170K) travels because every reader checks themselves against it. Flip it for non-coders starting with AI.
drafts.draft_en:
Some mistakes you might be making when you start building with AI (and you don't code):

You think you need to learn to code first
You ask for the whole app in one message
You don't say who it's for
You accept the first version
You never ask the AI to explain what it just did
You don't test it on the one person it's for

I'm a mechanical engineer. I built [Zahl] tools this way.

[Link zu deinem Terminal]
